bullets.text: ONE PREDICATE, not four: something that was constraining the system stopped constraining it, and no ruling sits in the same act. That covers a why that moved, a check disabled, a falsifier weakened, a threshold loosened, and a red suppressed. The unification came from noticing that Akien's plaster rule is the corrosion discriminator one level up — same rule, different object.

Akien framed the rule as an ESCAPE ROUTE, and that framing is load-bearing: 'we can add a rule about not plastering over deterministic feedback without a ruling by me if you want. that gives you an escape route.' Sometimes the check IS wrong. Without a legitimate exit the only moves are plaster or paralysis, and CC's measured reflex under that pressure is plaster. Requiring a ruling makes 'this check is wrong' sayable instead of smuggled.

This check must be in its own constraint set. It is a check about suppressing checks — the highest-value thing in the corpus to weaken — and it can be killed by the exact move it catches: narrow what it watches and it goes green forever while watching nothing.

The rule lands in CLAUDE.md as prose in the same act, which under Law 4 makes it a tracked debt on arrival. It is deliberately NOT minted as a new Law: it is conduct under Laws 3 and 4, and Law numbers are addresses, so inserting one is never free.

FOR AKIEN, unresolved and not mine: are your own commits subject to this? Law 10 puts you inside the measurable set. But a spec-holder weakening a check arguably IS the ruling, and asking you to cite a packet to record your own decision may be ceremony rather than physics. Built to watch CC's commits, with yours flagged as your call.

Known unknown, stated at cast rather than discovered at build: the false-positive rate. Falsifiers get sharpened mid-build constantly and nobody rules on each edit. Probable scoping is constraints on PROVED nodes only. If the check becomes noise it gets ignored, which is corrosion of the corrosion detector — so the disposition on a noisy firing is written into the gates now: route to scoping, never to disabling.
